title: Influence of Resistance Training Proximity-to-Failure on Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis
population: 15 studies in healthy adults of any age and training experience.
key_findings: Pooling every definition of set failure, training to failure gave a trivial hypertrophy advantage over stopping short (effect size 0.19, confidence interval 0.00 to 0.37).
Training to momentary muscular failure was not better than non-failure training (effect size 0.12, interval -0.13 to 0.37), and high velocity-loss thresholds were not better than moderate ones.
The authors propose that the relationship between proximity to failure and growth may be non-linear.
methods: Systematic review and meta-analysis comparing failure with non-failure training, with subgroups by the definition of failure and by velocity-loss threshold; volume load and relative load tested as moderators.
limitations: Studies defined failure inconsistently, which forced subgroup analyses; few studies per subgroup.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
